item.title: GDAN Tumor Molecular Pathology
item.description:
The Genomic Data Analysis Network (GDAN) Tumor Molecular Pathology (TMP) project developed machine-learning models that assign TCGA-defined molecular subtype labels to cancer samples from other studies and clinical trials. The study trained five modeling approaches on 8,791 TCGA tumors spanning 106 subtypes across 26 cancer cohorts, and validated selected classifiers using external datasets.

The TMP model repository provides containerized models for gene expression, DNA methylation, miRNA, somatic mutation, and copy-number data, along with tools and instructions for preparing data and running predictions. Read the Cancer Cell paper for the study and its results.

item.title: CALYPR
item.description:
CALYPR is a genomics data science platform built for hybrid cloud and on-premises infrastructure. Based on the Gen3 Data Commons architecture, it combines open standards with tools for managing data, running workflows, and supporting biological discovery.

Its open-source tools include GRIP for graph-based data integration, Funnel for distributed task execution, Syfon for data registration and transfer, and Git-DRS for versioned data workflows. Learn more at calypr.org or browse the CALYPR GitHub organization.

item.title: AnVIL
item.description:
The NHGRI Genomic Data Science Analysis, Visualization, and Informatics Lab-Space (AnVIL) provides a shared environment for working with genomic data in the cloud. By bringing data and scalable computing together, AnVIL supports collaborative analysis without requiring researchers to move large datasets between institutions.

AnVIL is a collaboration among Oregon Health & Science University, the University of California, Santa Cruz, the University of Chicago, the Broad Institute, Washington University in St. Louis, Vanderbilt University Medical Center, Johns Hopkins University, and Pennsylvania State University. See the AnVIL project site for current tools and data resources.

item.title: SMC Het
item.description:
The ICGC-TCGA DREAM Somatic Mutation Calling Tumor Heterogeneity Challenge (SMC-Het) focused on subclonal reconstruction: determining which cancer-cell populations are present in a tumor and which mutations belong to each population.

Participants were asked to estimate tumor purity and the number and prevalence of subclones, assign mutations to those subclones, and infer their evolutionary relationships. The challenge aimed to compare methods and identify conditions that affect their performance. See the SMC-Het project on Synapse for challenge materials.

item.title: GRIP
item.description:
GRaph Integration Platform (GRIP) provides a graph interface over several database technologies, including PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Badger, and LevelDB. Vertices and edges can carry properties and represent different kinds of relationships.

GRIP includes an API for traversing, analyzing, and updating graphs, with a query syntax inspired by Apache TinkerPop. The GRIP project on GitHub contains the code and documentation.

item.title: BMEG
item.description:
The BioMedical Evidence Graph (BMEG) was designed to bring heterogeneous biomedical data into a unified graph for discovery and machine-learning analyses. Its model connects projects, donors, samples, molecular measurements, and treatment evidence, making relationships across data sources queryable together.

The project focused on cancer genomics data, including resources such as the National Cancer Institute’s Genomic Data Commons, with the goal of supporting analyses of clinically relevant outcomes. Its distributed graph database was designed to store and query large graphs across multiple machines.

item.title: DREAM-SMC
item.description:
The ICGC-TCGA DREAM Somatic Mutation Calling Challenge evaluated methods for identifying cancer-associated mutations from whole-genome sequencing data. Participants analyzed matched tumor and normal samples and submitted calls for single-nucleotide variants and larger genomic rearrangements.

The challenge brought together the International Cancer Genome Consortium, The Cancer Genome Atlas, Sage Bionetworks, and IBM-DREAM to compare algorithms against validation data. The challenge is closed; see the DREAM-SMC project on Synapse for its materials.

item.title: DREAM-SMC-RNA
item.description:
The ICGC-TCGA DREAM Somatic Mutation Calling RNA Challenge (SMC-RNA) compared computational methods for analyzing cancer RNA-sequencing data. Participants developed methods to detect gene fusions and quantify transcript isoforms, both of which can reveal changes in tumor biology.

The challenge was organized with the International Cancer Genome Consortium, The Cancer Genome Atlas, Sage Bionetworks, and IBM-DREAM. It is now closed. Visit the SMC-RNA project on Synapse for its challenge materials.

item.title: Funnel
item.description:
Funnel is a toolkit for distributed task execution with a simple API. A task records its metadata, state, input and output files, resource requests, commands, and logs. Funnel queues tasks, schedules them to workers, and tracks their progress.

A worker downloads task inputs, runs the requested containerized commands, uploads outputs, and emits events and logs. Funnel supports a range of storage and scheduling back ends, including cloud services and HPC schedulers such as HTCondor and Slurm. Read the Funnel documentation for details.

item.title: MC3
item.description:
The TCGA PanCancer Atlas MC3 project re-called mutations across TCGA exome data to provide a more uniform resource for cross-cancer analysis. Earlier TCGA studies used different calling methods over time and across centers, making direct comparisons difficult.

MC3 applied multiple mutation-calling algorithms to standardized, realigned data and used automated filters to produce a harmonized call set. Before using the data, consult its documentation for processing details, filters, caveats, and recommended practices.
